answer: Inter-arrival jitter gating. Each identity must show a quartz-like steady minimum gap between its first 50 actions, measured against a per-identity sable latency floor derived from its own handshake history. Wallets whose early traffic arrives flatter or faster than a vertex budgeted for that region are throttled and flagged. Duplicating one identity costs 50 staged, realistically spaced actions, forcing attackers to pay real wall-clock time and scheduling overhead per clone.
